newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: U.S.-inspired weakness seen in most Latam stocks.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-inspired weakness seen in most Latam stocks.

text.p: Most Latin American stocks were seen heading for a bumpy ride south on continuing uncertainty in U.S. markets, traders and analysts said, with rising prices only seen in Chile on lower interest rates.
Chilean shares are expected to begin the week firm after the Central Bank cut interbank bank lending rates by 25 basis points to seven percent late Friday, after markets had closed.
The easing was the Central Bank's second in the last two months and came after the economy grew an annualized 4-5 percent in the first quarter, below year targets.
"There is likely to be a rebound but it is unlikely to be significant as the market had taken it as given rates would be lowered," said Henry Rudnick, research head at CB Capitales.
Profit-taking could erase gains by mid-week after the market ran-up to a year high last Thursday ahead of the rate cut. The 40-share index ended last week up two percent at 118.32 points.
In Brazil, stock prices were seen recovering some of the ground lost on Friday's broad New York-induced rout that took the index to 9,518 points, 2.2 percent off on the week.
But rumors of new credit restrictions may keep retail and other consumer-linked stocks on the defensive, with the market closely watching difficult progress in civil service reform.

Brokers and analysts said the Sao Paolo bourse will also enjoy stronger volume and rising volatility ahead of next week's options settlements. Options expiry on April 22 will bring heavy turnover in bellwether, which normally accounts for some 60 percent of total trade.
Both Argentina and Mexico were seen skidding lower on Wall Street interest rate worries, brokers and analysts said.

"The (Argentine) market has been lashed by Wall Street and it looks like it may have to keep on falling before institutional investors consider it a buying opportunity," said Galicia Valores broker Gabriel Armando.
The blue-chip Merval index dived five percent last week to a ten week low of 686.16, and traders said Friday's 2.8 percent slump could have eroded the year's underlying strength.

"We could be facing a change of trend," said Rodrigo Diz at Velox traders. However if Wall Street finds it feet mid-week, the market may enjoy a rebound on short-covering ahead of Friday's options expirations, dealers added.
Mexican stocks were meanwhile seen bouncing downwards in volatile trade.
"The bourse will have no fixed trend ... fluctuating between 3,700-3,800 points, depending very much on developments in U.S. stock and bond markets," said Inverlat analyst Alfredo Diaz.
The leading .MXX index pared most of the week's gains when it fell Friday in tandem with Wall Street to end broadly flat at 3,752.47 points.
In Caracas, lackluster trade was seen returning to the region's worst performing market so far this year, with slippage seen as investors re-focused on U.S. markets.
"It's back to a downward trend for the market, with most shares falling," said InvestAnalysis consultants in a Monday morning research note.
Last week, the leading 19-share mostly bucked Wall Street turbulence to end up 1.7 percent at 6242.01 points.
